name: Winery / tasting room
summary: Ground-up winery building combining a hospitality tasting room (bar, retail, restrooms, catering pantry) with production space (crush/fermentation, barrel room, case goods) on a rural parcel with an event lawn. Cost depends on the hospitality share and finish level (destination wineries are architect-designed), plus rural infrastructure (well, on-site wastewater, long drives). Evidence is limited: two Texas Hill Country accessibility registrations (2021, 2023) at ~$370–400/SF and one California project listing at ~$1,900/SF (outlier); the rest is derived from restaurant and industrial proxies.

typicalSize.method: Siboney Cellars winery + tasting room 10,720 SF (v1); Portree Cellars tasting facility 5,000 SF (v2); Delfino winery & tasting room 3,078 SF + 3,658 SF covered crush pad (v3). Mid 8,000 SF for a combined boutique winery; high for 20k+ case production.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Building SF per acre of the developed winery pad (excluding vineyard): building + parking + event lawn + crush pad on 2–5 acres. Judgment.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: Tasting/assembly portion parked like a bar or event space; production lightly parked. Often gravel overflow lots for events. Judgment.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Evidence years 2019 (v3), 2021 (v1), 2023 (v2); range expressed in 2023 dollars. Texas Hill Country registrations: Siboney Cellars winery + tasting $3,965,000 / 10,720 SF = $370/SF (v1, 2021, includes production and barrel room); Portree Cellars tasting facility with pavilion $1,994,960 / 5,000 SF = $399/SF (v2, 2023, hospitality-heavy). Texas costs run below national, offsetting registration under-reporting → mid $400/SF. Low $250 = pre-engineered production-heavy building with a modest tasting bar (cf. industrial proxy bar-brewery-taproom.json#b1 scaled); high $750 = architect-designed destination tasting room (restaurant-grade FOH, restaurant-full-service.json#r1-type finishes). Delfino Winery (Camino, CA) $12.9M / 6,736 SF ≈ $1,915/SF (v3) is recorded but treated as an outlier (likely includes major site/infrastructure and bespoke design).

scope.notes: Building (tasting room, production, barrel room with insulated envelope and humidity control, restrooms, catering pantry) plus typical on-site work (drive, parking, utilities within the property, landscaping around building). Excludes winemaking equipment and tanks, covered crush pad, event lawn, rural wastewater/well systems (line items), FF&E, land, vineyard, soft costs, off-site road/utility extensions.

qualityTiers.method: low/mid (250/400 ≈ 0.63) and high/mid (750/400 ≈ 1.9 as luxury); premium 1.4 interpolated. Delfino (v3) shows destination projects can exceed even the luxury tier.

systemSplit.method: Derived from bar-brewery-taproom split: heavier 07 (insulated barrel-room envelope), 06 (wood finishes in tasting room), 23 (barrel-room cooling/humidification, glycol rough-in); lighter kitchen plumbing. Site 0.17. Not from a published estimate.

lineItems.name: Winemaking equipment (destemmer/crusher, press, stainless tanks, pumps, glycol, barrels)

cost.method: Judgment for a 2,000–20,000 case winery; scales with tank capacity. Older anecdotal small-winery packages ($60–120k, 2010) are not used. Verify with equipment vendor quotes.

lineItems.notes: Omit for tasting-room-only projects (no on-site production).

lineItems.name: Covered crush pad (slab with trench drains + open-sided roof)

cost.method: Delfino program includes a 3,658 SF covered crush pad (v3); unit cost is judgment (pre-engineered canopy + heavy slab + trench drains).

lineItems.name: On-site process + sanitary wastewater system and well (rural sites)

cost.method: Judgment: winery process wastewater (high-strength, seasonal) usually needs pretreatment and land application or engineered septic when no sewer is available, plus a commercial well and storage. Highly site/state specific — verify.

lineItems.notes: Switch on when the site has no public sewer/water.

lineItems.name: Event lawn and landscape (grading, irrigation, turf, lighting, paths)

cost.method: Judgment for irrigated turf with festoon lighting and hardscape paths.

lineItems.notes: Catalog description includes an event lawn; switch on when programmed. Portree (v2) included a pavilion within its reported cost.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Tasting-room furniture, bar equipment, retail fixtures, POS and signage spread over gross SF (hospitality ≈ 30–50% of area). Judgment, cf. restaurant-full-service FF&E $100–270/SF of FOH-heavy area.

pctOfHard.method: Higher than urban commercial because of rural entitlements (agricultural/event use permits), civil design for wells/wastewater, and architect-led design for destination tasting rooms. Judgment.

softCosts.notes: Type-specific: TTB bonded winery permit, state winery/tasting licenses, conditional/special use permits for events.

perPrimaryUnit.method: Hard $250–750 × 1.10–1.20; max widened toward destination projects like v3. Excludes equipment, vineyard and land.

source.title: TABS project TABS2021016345 — Siboney Cellars Phase II
source.publisher: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation

evidence.quote: New construction of a 10,720 sf winery and tasting room housing a production facility, barrel room, and tasting areas. … Estimated Cost: $3,965,000
evidence.scopeNotes: $370/SF; start 12/1/2020, completion 11/1/2021. Self-reported registration estimate; site scope unknown.

source.title: TABS project TABS2024003484 — Portree Cellars Tasting Room
source.publisher: Texas Department of Licensing and Regulation

evidence.quote: New Construction, ground-up, 5,000 SF Wine Tasting Facility with Pavilion … Estimated Cost: $1,994,960

evidence.scopeNotes: 3,078 SF winery & tasting room + 3,658 SF covered crush pad; ≈$1,915/SF. Scope of the $12.9M (site, infrastructure, other buildings) not stated — treated as an outlier.

openQuestions: Only Texas registrations and one California listing found — web search quota ran out. Seek county planning staff reports for winery use permits (Napa, Sonoma, Paso Robles, Willamette Valley) that state construction valuation.
Winemaking equipment, crush pad, rural wastewater and event lawn costs are judgment values.
Split between tasting-room and production costs is not separated by any source.
